_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); machinery and engines signals

pit_profile.why: 'Caterpillar is the world’s leading manufacturer of construction and mining equipment, diesel and natural gas engines, industrial gas turbines and diesel-electric locomotives' (FY2015 10-K, Item 1); 'Caterpillar products and product support services are sold worldwide into a variety of highly competitive markets'; 'The demand for our products and services tends to be cyclical and can be significantly reduced in an economic environment characterized by lower levels of government and business investment, lower levels of business confidence, lower corporate earnings, perceived or actual industry overcapacity, higher unemployment and lower consumer spending.', 'The energy and mining industries are major users of our products, including the coal, iron ore, gold, copper, oil and natural gas industries.' and 'Changes in environmental and climate change laws or regulations, including laws relating to greenhouse gas emissions, could lead to new or additional investment in product designs and could increase environmental compliance expenditures.' (Item 1A): the 10-K calls the demand for its own products cyclical (BKR's 'Our business is cyclical'), so CYCLICAL from the FY2010 10-K; ENERGY_TRANSITION is live from 2015-12-12 but scoped to oil, gas and coal reserves and refining, which a maker of construction and mining equipment, engines and turbines does not hold, so the climate-change wording stays here

classification.quality_note: 'Caterpillar is the world’s leading manufacturer of construction and mining equipment, diesel and natural gas engines, industrial gas turbines and diesel-electric locomotives' (FY2015 10-K, Item 1); 'Caterpillar products and product support services are sold worldwide into a variety of highly competitive markets'; 'The demand for our products and services tends to be cyclical and can be significantly reduced in an economic environment characterized by lower levels of government and business investment, lower levels of business confidence, lower corporate earnings, perceived or actual industry overcapacity, higher unemployment and lower consumer spending.', 'The energy and mining industries are major users of our products, including the coal, iron ore, gold, copper, oil and natural gas industries.' and 'Changes in environmental and climate change laws or regulations, including laws relating to greenhouse gas emissions, could lead to new or additional investment in product designs and could increase environmental compliance expenditures.' (Item 1A): the 10-K calls the demand for its own products cyclical (BKR's 'Our business is cyclical'), so CYCLICAL from the FY2010 10-K; ENERGY_TRANSITION is live from 2015-12-12 but scoped to oil, gas and coal reserves and refining, which a maker of construction and mining equipment, engines and turbines does not hold, so the climate-change wording stays here. cyclical (obsolescence risk 2/5); price rich; +71% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap -2.02; conservative 2yr -17%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -61.5%/yr (worst year FY06-FY15, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +-9.2%/yr (FY16 guide + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +-1.2%/yr (FY06-FY15 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +84.2%/yr (best 2-yr run FY06-FY15); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: CAT (retrospective, 2016-03-24) ✕ AVOID — Ratio B infx (92.0% downside to Bear $6 / +-16.3% upside to Bull $63) | Adj composite 0.95 vs market 2.97: gap -2.02 [OVERVALUED] | +71% above the EPP floor $44 (11x FY16E $4.00) | Conservative 2-yr case: -17.2% total (-8.6%/yr) | At 18.8x FY16E the 15% hurdle price $100 sits above the BULL case; Machinery sales -19.5% in Q4 2015, forward revenues -14.9% to -6.4% (FY16 sales and revenues guide); ENERGY_TRANSITION is live from 2015-12-12 but scoped to oil, gas and coal reserves and refining; no theme in scope has dated evidence.

sources.title: Caterpillar FY2015 10-K
sources.supports: 2011-2015 sales and revenues and profit per share - diluted (five-year summary), 2013-2015 statement of results, 2014-2015 external sales by segment, 2015 cash, operating cash flow and dividends; Items 1 and 1A

sources.title: Caterpillar 8-K: fourth-quarter 2015 results release
sources.supports: fourth-quarter 2015 sales and revenues by segment and statement of results, full-year 2015 actuals; 2016 outlook: sales and revenues $40 to $44 billion, profit $4.00 per share excluding restructuring costs (about $3.50 including them)

sources.title: Caterpillar 8-K, Items 2.05 and 7.01: restructuring and cost reduction plans (Exhibit 99.1)
sources.supports: 2015 sales and revenues outlook about $48 billion (no profit outlook); 2016 sales and revenues about 5 percent below 2015

sources.title: Caterpillar 8-K: third-quarter 2015 results release
sources.supports: third-quarter 2015 sales and revenues by segment and statement of results; 2015 outlook: sales and revenues about $48 billion, profit $4.60 per share excluding restructuring costs (about $3.70 including them); preliminary 2016 sales and revenues down about 5 percent

sources.title: Caterpillar 8-K: 'Caterpillar Splits Stock; Increases Dividend Rate'
sources.supports: a two-for-one stock split; the split shares distributed on July 13 to stockholders of record on June 22, 2005
